en: On the bank of the Bhīmarathī, at the seat of Mahāyoga,
the lords of sages gathered and remained there, bestowing a boon upon Puṇḍarīka, as they dwelt in that source of bliss.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 1.
Clad in lightning, with the luster of a dark cloud,
the beautiful abode of Ramā, manifesting pure consciousness;
the Supreme Lord, with his feet placed upon the sacrificial brick.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 2.
This hip of mine is the proof that the Creator held the ocean of existence with his two hands;
for it was from him that the navel-cavity was taken to serve as his dwelling place.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 3.
Adorned with the shimmering Kaustubha gem upon his neck,
graced by Śrī, wearing armlets, the abode of Fortune— auspicious, peaceful, praiseworthy, excellent, and the guardian of the world.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 4.
With a face like the orb of the autumn moon, a beautiful smile, and the regions of her cheeks adorned with shimmering earrings;
with lips like the red Bimba fruit of the Japā flower and lotus-like eyes.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 5.
His crown illuminates the furthest reaches of every direction;
he is worshipped by the gods with priceless divine jewels; his form is characterized by the triple bend (tribhaṅga), and he is adorned with a crest of peacock feathers and garlands.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman.
The all-pervading Lord, whose flute-song is boundless, who wanders at will assuming the guise of a cowherd out of his own sport,
bestowing joy upon the herds of cows with his beautiful smile.
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman.
To that unborn one, the restorer of Rukmiṇī’s life, the supreme abode, the unique absolute, the fourth state—
to that gracious God of gods, the destroyer of the distress of those who seek refuge;
I worship Pāṇḍuraṅga, the emblem of the Supreme Brahman. 8.
Those who daily recite this hymn to Pāṇḍuraṅga with single-minded devotion shall,
at the time of their end, cross over the ocean of worldly existence.
They attain the eternal abode of Hari. 9.

Thus ends "The Eight Verses on Paṇḍuraṅga," composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (Paramahaṃsa Parivrājakācārya).
